name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor that does not exceed 750 watts, in one of three classes: pedal-assist to 20 mph, throttle-capable to 20 mph, or pedal-assist to 28 mph with a speedometer. Defined by California Vehicle Code §312.5, as amended by SB 1271 (Chapter 791, Statutes of 2024), and regulated by §§21207.5 (as amended by AB 1909, Chapter 343, Statutes of 2022), 21212, 21213 and 24016.

restrictions.rule: Fully operable pedals and an electric motor that does not exceed 750 watts
A Class 1 or Class 3 motor can't propel it on its own; Class 1 and Class 2 stop assisting at 20 mph, Class 3 at 28 mph, and a Class 3 must have a speedometer
Not an electric bicycle once modified so the motor alone can exceed 20 mph, the motor exceeds 750 watts, or the pedals are removed
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage; it may be modified only if it still meets the definition and its label is replaced to match
No one may sell a product, device or app that changes an electric bicycle's speed so it no longer meets the definition
Must meet the CPSC's bicycle requirements, and its motor must cut out when the brakes are applied or a switch is released
Since January 1, 2026, may only be sold with a battery tested by an accredited laboratory and marked with that laboratory's name or logo
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration, license plate or insurance

Riders under 18 must wear a bicycle helmet; on a Class 3, every rider and passenger must wear one; a minor's helmet ticket is excused by proof of a helmet and completion of the CHP's e-bike safety course
Riders must be 16 or older to ride a Class 3, and since January 1, 2026 a Class 3 can't be sold to anyone under 16
Must show a red reflector, or a solid or flashing red light with a built-in reflector, on the rear at all times, not only after dark

Ridden wherever bicycles may go, Class 3 included: since January 1, 2023 no class is barred from bike paths, bikeways or bike lanes, though a local authority may ban any class from an equestrian, hiking or recreational trail it manages, and State Parks from any bicycle path or trail
No city or county may require it to be licensed
A 10 mph prima facie speed limit on sidewalks, and a local authority may set a 10, 15 or 20 mph limit on a bike path or multiuse trail

Anything that can exceed 20 mph on a throttle or 28 mph with pedal assist can't be sold or advertised as an electric bicycle, and is a moped or motor-driven cycle instead; its label must name the brand and the manufacturer, importer or distributor
Every new Class 2 must have a speedometer, and every new electric bicycle front and rear lamps
Cities in San Mateo County may bar riders under 12 from Class 1 and Class 2 electric bicycles
